details: Council staff recap
headline: SLC Council questions HF Sinclair pipeline, delays Parry Block discounted sale
title: October 13, 2026 Meeting Recap
why_it_matters: On Oct. 13 the council was briefed by HF Sinclair on the proposed Westline Connect Pipeline and issued a joint statement with the mayor. Concerns raised included drinking water, the watershed and seismic risk. As the CRA board it approved support for HomeInn Rio Grande transitional housing and funding for six commercial projects, and asked for more discussion of a discounted Parry Block land sale.

details: Council staff recap
headline: SLC approves first utility impact fee update since 1999, flood aid
title: October 6, 2026 Meeting Recap
why_it_matters: On Oct. 6 the council approved new water, sewer and stormwater impact fees, the first update since 1999. Its budget amendment included $50,000 in emergency aid for Poplar Grove families flooded by a main break. It also took public comment on selling about 900 acres of surplus wetlands to Utah DNR with a conservation easement.

details: Meeting held 2026-05-05; minutes approved and posted later
headline: May minutes detail split votes suspending Lopez Chavez's council duties
names: Housing Authority of Salt Lake City
title: Minutes: Revised LBA, CRA and Council Formal Meeting, May 05, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of May 5 show the council voted 6-0, with Petro abstaining, to have an investigator probe allegations about Council Member Eva Lopez Chavez. It then voted 5-0, with Petro and Lopez Chavez abstaining, to suspend her leadership and speaking duties. The camping ordinance drew dozens of mostly opposed speakers and was deferred, and the 346 S 800 E rezone hearing was continued.

details: Meeting held 2026-05-19; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council dropped outside investigator in conduct probe, minutes show
names: Housing Authority of Salt Lake City
title: Minutes: LBA, CRA and Council Formal Meeting, May 19, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of May 19 show the council voted 6-0 to repurpose its working group to review the code of conduct, saying an independent investigator was no longer appropriate. Planning Commission and Landmark appointments for Kevin Chung and Rosemary Stum were pulled from consent. The council approved the Mansell Manor and 2260-2290 E 1300 S rezones 6-0.

details: Meeting held 2026-06-02; minutes approved and posted later
headline: June 2 budget hearing minutes posted
title: Minutes: LBA, CRA and Council Formal Meeting, Jun 02, 2026
why_it_matters: Routine minutes of budget public hearings; the council adopted only the Inland Port police item from Budget Amendment No. 5.

details: Meeting held 2026-06-16; minutes approved and posted later
editor_note: Months-old budget straw polls on police drones; useful context but not urgent.
headline: Council split on police drone pilot, license readers in June budget straw polls
title: Minutes: Council Work Session Meeting, Jun 16, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of the June 16 work session show a 3-4 straw poll rejecting full funding for a police drone pilot position, later cut to about five months. The council voted 6-1 to accept an ALPR subgrant and 5-2 to restore police leadership training, and moved drone funding into the property tax proposal 5-2.

details: Meeting held 2026-07-14; minutes approved and posted later
editor_note: Past CRA vote on tax increment deal; worth a brief, not urgent today.
headline: CRA approved Silo Park tax increment deal 6-1, Puy dissenting
names: Silos South BCG LPG Partners LLC
title: Minutes: Community Reinvestment Agency (CRA) Meeting, Jul 14, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of the July 14 CRA meeting show a 6-1 vote, Alejandro Puy opposed, approving a tax increment reimbursement agreement for the Silo Park Development. The board also approved a $2 million disaster relief loan to Chenzo LLC to rebuild fire-damaged 319-321 South Main Street.

details: Meeting held 2026-07-14; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council corrected tax levy ordinance after technical error, July minutes show
title: Minutes: Council Formal Meeting, Jul 14, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of July 14 show the council voted 5-0 to adopt a corrected tax levy ordinance after a technical error in Ordinance 28. Residents pressed for changes to short-term rental caps and for action on a disputed Parkway Avenue open-space parcel owned by South Salt Lake.

details: Meeting held 2026-07-21; minutes approved and posted later
headline: July work session minutes cover ALPR rules, water cap, Northwest plan
title: Minutes: Council Work Session Meeting, Jul 21, 2026
why_it_matters: Pending minutes of July 21 detail briefings on a police license plate reader ordinance, the 200,000-gallon daily water cap and the Northwest Community Plan. A report showed only two affordable housing incentive projects completed. No votes were taken.

details: Meeting held 2026-08-18; minutes approved and posted later
headline: CRA approved Peacock Blocks demolition, $1M Main Street fire loan
title: Minutes: Community Reinvestment Agency (CRA) Meeting, Aug 18, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of the Aug. 18 CRA meeting show the board backed $450,000 to demolish the Peacock Blocks at 400 South and 900 West. It approved a $1 million disaster loan to 323 LLC for the former Whiskey Street building, a library tax increment fix and a Sedona Apartments loan extension.

details: Meeting held 2026-08-18; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council split on new park restroom funding in August CIP straw polls
title: Minutes: Council Work Session Meeting, Aug 18, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of the Aug. 18 work session show unanimous support for phasing in utility impact fees at 70% until July 2028. Straw polls split 5-2 and 4-3 over funding a $568,000 new park restroom.

details: Meeting held 2026-08-18; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Sugar House property owners opposed assessment at August hearing
title: Minutes: Council Formal Meeting, Aug 18, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of Aug. 18 show business owners and the Utah Restaurant Association opposed the Sugar House assessment, citing construction losses; that proposal has since been dropped. Ballpark neighbors pressed for green space, and George LeBoeuf's appointment was pulled from consent. The council approved the Via Veneto liquor waiver and the mobile business ordinance 7-0.

details: Meeting held 2026-08-25; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council pulled Northwest Community Plan vote, adopted CIP in August
title: Minutes: Council Formal Meeting, Aug 25, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of Aug. 25 show the Northwest Community Plan vote was moved to a future meeting and CIP allocations were adopted 6-0. Hearings were set on a Northpoint industrial rezone the Planning Commission opposed and an Intermountain Health alley vacation.

details: Meeting held 2026-09-08; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council backed mailing on housing options proposal; airport wetland sale briefed
title: Minutes: Council Work Session Meeting, Sep 08, 2026
why_it_matters: Pending minutes of the Sept. 8 work session show unanimous support for mailing residents about the Expanding Housing Options proposal. The council was briefed on selling about 900 acres of airport wetlands to Utah DNR with a Utah Open Lands easement, then held a closed attorney-client session.

details: Meeting held 2026-09-08; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council extended 247 North 800 West rezone deadline
title: Minutes: Council Limited Formal Meeting, Sep 08, 2026
why_it_matters: Routine minutes; one-year extension approved 6-0 and impact fee hearings set.

details: Meeting held 2026-09-15; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council adopted daily water-use cap, Ivory Innovations fee waiver in September
title: Minutes: Council Formal Meeting, Sep 15, 2026
why_it_matters: Minutes of Sept. 15 show a 7-0 vote making the 200,000-gallon daily water cap permanent, with a request for a study of lowering it. The council approved a fee waiver for Ivory Innovations' 66-unit project at 707 South 400 East, and the ALPR hearing was rescheduled.

details: Meeting held 2026-10-06; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Council held closed session on property purchase or lease Oct. 6
title: Minutes: Council Work Session Meeting, Oct 06, 2026
why_it_matters: Pending minutes of Oct. 6 show a closed session of more than an hour on the purchase, exchange or lease of real property and attorney-client matters. The public utilities director attended.

details: Council staff recap
headline: SLC Council approves Ballpark zoning, bans jails and correctional facilities on private property
title: October 20, 2026 Meeting Recap
why_it_matters: At its Oct. 20, 2026 meeting, the council approved new Ballpark NEXT zoning regulations and prohibited community correctional facilities and jails on private property in the city. It also set Expanding Housing Options hearings for Nov. 10 and 17, and the Community Clean Energy Program is set to launch in January 2027.

details: Meeting held 2026-09-08; minutes approved and posted later
editor_note: Minutes cover 900-acre airport wetland sale briefing; real news angle, keep visible.
headline: Minutes: Council briefed on 900-acre airport wetland sale, housing zoning changes
title: Minutes: Council Work Session Meeting, Sep 08, 2026
why_it_matters: These are official minutes of the Sept. 8 work session, which included a briefing on the 900-acre airport wetland sale to DNR and an Expanding Housing Options mailer straw poll. The closed session was for attorney-client matters, and the session was largely reported at the time.

details: Meeting held 2026-09-22; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Minutes show Northpoint rezone deferred amid truck concerns; pipeline opposition aired
title: Minutes: Council Formal Meeting, Sep 22, 2026
why_it_matters: Pending Sept. 22 minutes show the council deferred the Northpoint industrial rezone; the ordinance version noted an added data center prohibition, and the Planning Commission had recommended against it. Speakers including Rep. Angela Romero opposed a potential Sinclair/Phillips 66 pipeline. The minutes also record a 0-0 all-abstain vote on the Hispanic Heritage resolution and the Cowdell appeals officer appointment pulled from consent; the 1990 S 500 E townhome rezone passed 7-0.

details: Meeting held 2026-10-06; minutes approved and posted later
headline: Minutes: Council held closed session on real property purchase or lease
title: Minutes: Council Work Session Meeting, Oct 06, 2026
why_it_matters: Official minutes of the Oct. 6 work session. Interviews were held for board appointees, and the council met in a 77-minute closed session on real property and attorney-client matters.
